components.name: Progress Rail

narrative.overview: Attesta reads like an official registry document, not a consumer app. Every screen is a ruled ledger: a label in the left margin, a measured value entered on the line, and a verdict resolved at the right. The technician is not filling a form — they are reading an installation against a published standard and recording the result, one row at a time. Type is a compact grotesque for prose paired with a tabular monospace for every label, value, and verdict, so columns of numbers align and a measured value reads as data. The system refuses the soft rounded SaaS wizard with a floating purple button; it is flat, ruled, and square because the document it produces is.
keyCharacteristics: Archival-paper ground with near-black ink; one signal red for control/warning.
Tabular monospace for all labels, values, and verdicts; grotesque for prose.
Square corners, zero radius, no drop shadows — depth via hairlines and tonal bands.
The measurement row as the recurring signature: value → verdict (OK / NON OK).
Fixed progress rail and fixed footer; the working area alone scrolls.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal red appears on ≤10% of any screen. It marks only control, focus, warning, or a NON OK verdict. If everything is red, nothing is.

rules.name: The Green-Only-Verdict Rule
rules.body: Verdict green is never used for branding, success toasts, or decoration — only a measurement row resolving to OK.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Anything the technician measures, enters, or reads back as a value is set in IBM Plex Mono — never the proportional face.

rules.name: The Quiet Prose Rule
rules.body: Hints and explanatory text stay in Inter and stay short.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flush on the paper. Nothing floats. Separation is a hairline, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Lit-Edge Exception
rules.body: The only non-hairline emphasis is the measurement row's warning state, marked by an inset 3px signal-red left edge — a margin annotation, not a drop shadow.

dos: Do set every label, value, and verdict in IBM Plex Mono; reserve Inter for headings and one-line hints.
Do keep corners square (0px) and rely on 1px hairlines and the two tonal bands for all structure.
Do resolve each measurement row to an explicit OK / NON OK verdict.
Do hold the fixed header, footer, and progress rail steady while only the stage scrolls.
Do reserve signal red for control, focus, warning, or NON OK.
donts: Don't introduce drop shadows, border-radius, gradients, or pill shapes.
Don't set measured data in the proportional (Inter) face.
Don't use verdict green for anything except a resolved OK row.
Don't let the working area scroll the whole page or move the footer Continue button.
Don't invent a soft SaaS look (floating rounded buttons, card shadows, purple accents).
